newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn closes lower on late fund sale, weather.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn closes lower on late fund sale, weather.

text.p: CBOT corn futures closed lower on a late sale by Rosenthal Collins of five million bushels of March with bearish input from South American and U.S. weather cited as the key fundamentals, traders said.
"It was late fund selling in corn, Rosenthal sold five million," said Ron Kucha of O'Connor and Co.
Traders said the near-ideal weather in South America was weighing on the corn and soybean market while forecasts for warmer weather in the U.S. would trim feed usage by the nation's livestock herd.
Corn was firm in early dealings on export action.
But the volume was thin amid quiet holiday dealings which left the market vulnerable to rapid swings in prices.
"Sales (exports) gave us strength early but we're in a narrow trading range and light volume," Kucha said.

USDA early Friday said net export sales of U.S. corn during the week ended December 19 totaled 993,000 tonnes, above the previous week's tally of 700,800 and above trade expectations for 600,000 to 700,000 tonnes.
Corn closed unchanged to 2-1/2 cents per bushel lower, with March down 2-1/2 at $2.64-1/2.
Corn futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 25,000 contracts, below the 30,556 traded Thursday.
In corn options, FIMAT Futures bought 400 March $2.70 calls at 4-3/4 to five cents and LFG Futures bought 300 May $2.60 puts at 6-1/2 to seven cents, traders said.
Corn options volume was estimated by the CBOT at 5,000 contracts, below the 6,359 traded Thursday.
